question: Which of the soluble fibres found in fruits is used as a thickener in cooking and baking?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pectin.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pectin** is a **soluble fiber** found in** fruits** that is commonly used as a** thickener in cooking and baking.**
 
• It is particularly useful for **making jams and jellies **as it helps to set the **fruit mixture.**
 
• Pectin is also used in the food industry as a **stabilizer and emulsifier,** and it is found in many processed foods such as **yogurt, ice cream, and salad dressings.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Lignin** is also a type of fiber found in fruits, but it is** not soluble in water** and therefore cannot be used as a thickener.

 
 
• Lignin is a significant **organic polymer** that is widely distributed in the **cell walls **of some particular cells.
 
• It performs a wide range of biological tasks, including the **movement of water, mechanical support, and resistance** to various stresses.
 
 
 
• **Cellulose** is another type of fiber found in fruits, but it is also **not soluble in water **and is not commonly used as a thickener in cooking and baking.
 
 
• All plant cell walls contain cellulose, an** insoluble dietary fiber** made of **glucose polymers**.
 
• Foods that contain cellulose include** leafy green vegetables** like **kale, Brussels sprouts, and green peas.**
 
 
 
• **Inulin** is a **soluble fiber** found in some fruits and vegetables, but it is** not** commonly used as a thickener in cooking and baking.
 
 
• It is often used as a** prebiotic to promote gut health.**
 
• In the stomach, it is **neither digested nor absorbed.**
 
• It persists in the bowel and promotes the growth of specific a**dvantageous bacteria. **
